subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Chameleons can change their colour in an instant in order to blend with their background. They also have the ________ to move each of their eyes independently. They are also capable of looking in any direction. Chameleons feed on insects. They catch them with the help of their sticky tongue. Did you know: they can shoot out their tongue farther – more than the _________ of their own head and body combined!
solution:
"The correct answer is **'Option 3'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requiring completion is "Chameleons can change their colour in an instant in order to blend with their background. They also have the ________ to move each of their eyes independently. They are also capable of looking in any direction. Chameleons feed on insects. They catch them with the help of their sticky tongue. Did you know: they can shoot out their tongue farther – more than the _________ of their own head and body combined!"
 
• The first blank is asking for a term that describes a specific capability of chameleons, which is "ability" in option 3.
 
• The second blank is seeking a word that accurately describes a physical measurement, in this case, "length" in option 3 matches the context dutifully, referring to the distance the tongue can cover.
 
• Thus, the complete sentence reads, "Chameleons can change their colour in an instant in order to blend with their background. They also have the ability to move each of their eyes independently. They are also capable of looking in any direction. Chameleons feed on insects. They catch them with the help of their sticky tongue. Did you know: they can shoot out their tongue farther – more than the length of their own head and body combined!"

Therefore, the correct answer is** "Option 3."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: "power; breadth" Power could suggest a capability, but it doesn't fit as comfortably as 'ability.' Similarly, 'breadth' could mean a distance of covering space, but it's not specific to vertical or head-to-body ones, making it less accurate.
 
• Option 2: "means; width" 'Means' often refers to tangible resources, not a physical ability. The term 'width' may indicate distance but is more associated with horizontal measurement, making it less appropriate.
 
• Option 4: "propensity; span" Propensity refers more to inclination or natural tendency, not physical ability. Span can indicate distance, but it's not as precise in this context as 'length'.
